seoTitle: Free fetch() to cURL Converter - JavaScript to curl
metaDescription: Convert a JavaScript fetch(url, options) call into a curl command, including headers, method and JSON.stringify bodies. Free, nothing is executed.
intro: Converts a JavaScript fetch(url, { method, headers, body }) call into a curl command. It understands JSON.stringify bodies, string literals and object literals, and never runs your code.
why: A failing request in the browser is often easier to reproduce from a terminal: you can change headers, see raw responses and share a one-line command with a colleague. DevTools can copy a request as curl, but when you have only a code snippet, such as a fetch call from an issue, a tutorial or your own source, you have to rewrite it by hand. This tool reads the call as text and builds the equivalent command: the method, each header, and the body, including a body written with JSON.stringify of an object literal. It does not execute your code, so nothing in the snippet can run, and it stays in your browser. Features without a curl equivalent, such as credentials: "include", are ignored.
howTo: Paste the fetch(...) call, with its options object, into the input box.
Run the conversion to get the curl command.
Copy it into your terminal and replace any placeholder tokens before running it.

faq.a: No. The call is read as text and parsed with simple rules. Variables, function calls and template placeholders cannot be evaluated, so use literal values for the best result.
The URL, method, headers and body. A JSON.stringify of an object literal becomes a JSON body. Options with no curl equivalent, like credentials, mode or cache, are skipped.

faq.q: What if my body is built from variables?
faq.a: Replace the variables with sample values first. The tool can only convert what it can read as a literal.

faq.q: Can I go the other way?
faq.a: Yes, the cURL to Code tool and the other cURL converters on this site turn a curl command into fetch and other languages.
